To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a rational attacker can profit from a whale attack if the attacker has a sufficiently high probability of winning a fork race and the attacker’s probability of winning is sufficiently high.

(i) a whale transaction can be used to incentivize a blockchain fork; (ii) the probability of a fork occurring increases in the size of the whale transaction and the number of miners who participate in the fork; (iii) the expected payoff of the attacker is increasing in the size of their transaction, the number of miners that participate in the fork, and the fraction of mining power they control; (iv) if the number of miners is large and the attacker’s mining power is small
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can we incentivize miners to create forks in the Bitcoin blockchain?
the security of Bitcoin’s Nakamoto consensus protocol, which is the core innovation of the Bitcoin system.
the question of whether a whale attack on Bitcoin can cause a blockchain fork, and, if so, under what conditions it can be profitable for the attacker.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bitcoin blockchain is not secure in the sense that a whale attack can be used to fork the blockchain.
the whale attack is a viable threat to Bitcoin and other proof-of-work blockchains.
Bitcoin is not a secure currency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a rational miner should not fork the chain when the attacker has a whale transaction, and that a rational miner would not mine on a fork that includes a whale transaction.
a whale attack is a profitable attack when: (1) the attacker is a rational player, and (2) the attacker has enough money to pay for the whale transaction.
we show that the current fee market is not incentive compatible, and that the current market structure incentivizes whales to fork the chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Nakamoto consensus does not provide a probabilistic guarantee of security in a rational world.
, while Nakamoto consensus does provide a probabilistic guarantee of finality for transactions, this guarantee can be compromised by a rational miner.
the security of Bitcoin’s Nakamoto consensus can be compromised by rational miners, even if they are honest in the short-term.
